arxiv-1606-07277.title: Validation of the Replica Trick for Simple Models
arxiv-1606-07277.creator: Takashi Shinzato
arxiv-1606-07277.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Takashi Shinzato. We discuss replica analytic continuation using several simple models in order to prove mathematically the validity of replica analysis, which is used in a wide range of fields related to large scale complex systems. While replica analysis consists of two analytical techniques, the replica trick (or replica analytic continuation) and the thermodynamical limit (and/or order parameter expansion), we focus our study on replica analytic continuation, which is the mathematical basis of the replica trick.

arxiv-2012-05730.title: Two-loop corrections to the Higgs trilinear coupling in models with extended scalar sectors
arxiv-2012-05730.creator: Shinya Kanemura
arxiv-2012-05730.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Shinya Kanemura. The Higgs trilinear coupling provides a unique opportunity to study the structure of the Higgs sector and probe indirect signs of BSM Physics – even if new states are somehow hidden. In models with extended Higgs sectors, large deviations in the Higgs trilinear coupling can appear at one loop because of non-decoupling effects in the radiative corrections involving the additional scalar states. It is then natural to ask how two-loop corrections modify this result, and whether new large corrections can appear again.

arxiv-2012-15670.title: New method for renormalon subtraction using Fourier transform Journal: Physics Letters B
arxiv-2012-15670.creator: Y. Hayashi a , Y. Sumino a and H. Takaura b
arxiv-2012-15670.description: Abstract To improve accuracy in calculating QCD effects, we propose a method for renormalon subtraction in the context of the operator-product expansion. The method enables subtracting renormalons of various powers in Λ QCD \Lambda_{\rm QCD} efficiently and simultaneously from single-scale observables. We apply it to different observables and examine consistency with theoretical expectations.

arxiv-2112-08080.title: On the application of the SCD semismooth* Newton method to variational inequalities of the second kind
arxiv-2112-08080.creator: Helmut Gfrerer, Jiří V. Outrata, Jan Valdman
arxiv-2112-08080.description: Abstract Abstract. The paper starts with a description of the SCD (subspace containing derivative) mappings and the SCD semismooth ∗ Newton method for the solution of general inclusions. This method is then applied to a class of variational inequalities of the second kind. As a result, one obtains an implementable algorithm exhibiting a locally superlinear convergence.

arxiv-2211-00127.title: A three tile 6–fold golden–mean tiling
arxiv-2211-00127.creator: Sam Coates 1, Toranosuke Matsubara 2, Akihisa Koga 2
arxiv-2211-00127.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sam Coates 1, Toranosuke Matsubara 2, Akihisa Koga 2. We present a multi–edge–length aperiodic tiling which exhibits 6–fold rotational symmetry. The edge lengths of the tiling are proportional to 1: τ \tau , where τ \tau is the golden mean 1 + 5 2 \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2} . We show how the tiling can be generated using simple substitution rules for its three constituent tiles, which we then use to demonstrate the bipartite nature of the tiling vertices.

arxiv-2302-07211.title: The Kelley-Meka bounds for sets free of three-term arithmetic progressions
arxiv-2302-07211.creator: Thomas F. Bloom, Olof Sisask
arxiv-2302-07211.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Thomas F. Bloom, Olof Sisask. We give a self-contained exposition of the recent remarkable result of Kelley and Meka: if A ⊆ { 1 , … , N } A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\} has no non-trivial three-term arithmetic progressions then | A | ≤ exp ⁡ ( − c ​ ( log ⁡ N ) 1 / 12 ) ​ N , \lvert A\rvert\leq\exp(-c(\log N)^{1/12})N, where c > 0 c>0 is a constant.

arxiv-2302-10242.title: A bespoke multigrid approach for magnetohydrodynamics models of magnetized plasmas in PETSc
arxiv-2302-10242.creator: Mark F. Adams, Matthew G. Knepley
arxiv-2302-10242.description: Abstract Fully realizing the potential of multigrid solvers often requires custom algorithms for a given application model, discretizations and even regimes of interest, despite considerable effort from the applied math community to develop fully algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods for almost 40 years.

arxiv-2306-01125.title: Reconstruction Distortion of Learned Image Compression with Imperceptible Perturbations
arxiv-2306-01125.creator: Yang Sui, Zhuohang Li, Ding Ding, Xiang Pan, Xiaozhong Xu, Shan Liu, Zhenzhong Chen
arxiv-2306-01125.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yang Sui, Zhuohang Li, Ding Ding, Xiang Pan, Xiaozhong Xu, Shan Liu, Zhenzhong Chen. Learned Image Compression (LIC) has recently become the trending technique for image transmission due to its notable performance. Despite its popularity, the robustness of LIC with respect to the quality of image reconstruction remains under-explored.

arxiv-2311-10156.title: Algebraic Topological Networks via the Persistent Local Homology Sheaf Thanks: Qualcomm AI Research is an initiative of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
arxiv-2311-10156.creator: Gabriele Cesa, Arash Behboodi
arxiv-2311-10156.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce a novel approach based on algebraic topology to enhance graph convolution and attention modules by incorporating local topological properties of the data. To do so, we consider the framework of sheaf neural networks , which has been previously leveraged to incorporate additional structure into graph neural networks’ features and construct more expressive, non-isotropic messages.

arxiv-2402-14483.title: MR-ARL: Model Reference Adaptive Reinforcement Learning for Robustly Stable On-Policy Data-Driven LQR
arxiv-2402-14483.creator: Marco Borghesi, Alessandro Bosso, Giuseppe Notarstefano
arxiv-2402-14483.description: Abstract This article introduces a novel framework for data-driven linear quadratic regulator (LQR) design. First, we introduce a reinforcement learning paradigm for on-policy data-driven LQR, where exploration and exploitation are simultaneously performed while guaranteeing robust stability of the whole closed-loop system encompassing the plant and the control/learning dynamics.

arxiv-2405-18871.title: DFAMiner : Mining minimal separating DFAs from labelled samples
arxiv-2405-18871.creator: Daniele Dell’Erba, Yong Li, Sven Schewe
arxiv-2405-18871.description: Abstract We propose DFAMiner , a passive learning tool for learning minimal separating deterministic finite automata (DFA) from a set of labelled samples. Separating automata are an interesting class of automata that occurs generally in regular model checking and has raised interest in foundational questions of parity game solving.

arxiv-2411-01041.title: Spatial profiles of a reaction-diffusion epidemic model with nonlinear incidence mechanism and constant total population Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
arxiv-2411-01041.creator: Rui Peng, Rachidi Salako, Yixiang Wu
arxiv-2411-01041.description: Abstract This paper examines a susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) epidemic reaction-diffusion model with no-flux boundary conditions and constant total population. The infection mechanism in the model is described by a nonlinear term of the form S q ​ I p S^{q}I^{p} with 0 < p ≤ 1 0<p\leq 1 and q > 0 q>0 .

arxiv-2503-08543.title: BoundarEase: Fostering Constructive Community Engagement to Inform More Equitable Student Assignment Policies
arxiv-2503-08543.creator: Cassandra Overney, Cassandra Moe, Alvin Chang, Nabeel Gillani
arxiv-2503-08543.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cassandra Overney, Cassandra Moe, Alvin Chang, Nabeel Gillani. Public school districts across the United States (US) play a pivotal role in shaping access to quality education through their student assignment policies—most prominently, school attendance boundaries. Community engagement processes for changing such policies, however, are often opaque, cumbersome, and highly polarizing—hampering equitable access to quality schools in ways that can perpetuate disparities in achievement and future life outcomes.

arxiv-2509-02154.title: Conditional- t 3 t^{3} VAE: Equitable Latent Space Allocation for Fair Generation
arxiv-2509-02154.creator: Aymene Mohammed Bouayed, Samuel Deslauriers-Gauthier, Adrian Iaccovelli, David Naccache
arxiv-2509-02154.description: Abstract Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) with global priors mirror the training set’s class frequency in latent space, underrepresenting tail classes and reducing generative fairness on imbalanced datasets. While t 3 t^{3} VAE improves robustness via heavy-tailed Student’s t-distribution priors, it still allocates latent volume proportionally to the class frequency.

arxiv-2509-15183.title: Lepton models from non-holomorphic A 5 ′ A^{\prime}_{5} modular flavor symmetry
arxiv-2509-15183.creator: Cai-Chang Li a,b,c , Gui-Jun Ding d,e a School of Physics, Northwest University, Xi’an 710127, China b Shaanxi Key Laboratory for Theoretical Physics Frontiers, Xi’an 710127, China c NSFC-SPTP Peng Huanwu Center for Fundamental Theory, Xi’an 710127, China d Department of Modern Physics, University o
arxiv-2509-15183.description: Abstract Abstract In the framework of non-holomorphic modular invariance approach, we have systematically constructed all minimal lepton models based on the non-holomorphic A^{\prime}_{5} modular symmetry from a bottom-up approach. In these models, the Yukawa couplings are described by polyharmonic Maaß forms of integer weights at level N=5 .

arxiv-2601-00483.title: Prediction of a measurable sign change in the Casimir force using a magnetic fluid
arxiv-2601-00483.creator: Long Ma, Larissa Inácio, Dai-Nam Le, Lilia M. Woods, Mathias Boström
arxiv-2601-00483.description: Abstract We demonstrate quantum levitation controlled by Casimir forces acting between a polystyrene surface and a Teflon-coated metallic substrate immersed in a mixture of Toluene and magnetite particles. This system experiences repulsion-attraction transitions in the Casimir interaction for distances where the effect is measurable.

pmc-10553267.title: Human-hippo conflicts around Lake Tana Biosphere Reserve, Ethiopia: Vulnerability of hippopotamus in human-dominated landscape
pmc-10553267.creator: Zewdu Kifle, Workiyie Worie Assefa, Amera Moges, Frank O. Masese, Frank O. Masese, Frank O. Masese
pmc-10553267.description: Currently, the demand of the human population for more land, water, and other natural resources from wildlife habitats is increasing all over the world. Such intense human pressure results in conflict with wildlife and the impacts affect both parties negatively. The human-hippo conflict poses a serious problem for both local farmers’ livelihoods and hippo conservation.

pmc-10603528.title: Brain capital, ecological development and sustainable environments
pmc-10603528.creator: Agustin Ibanez, Harris Eyre
pmc-10603528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The importance of improving brain and mental health and developing sustainable environments is increasingly recognised. Understanding the syndemic interactions between these processes can help address contemporary societal challenges and foster global innovation. Here, we propose a green brain capital model that integrates environmental drivers of brain health and green skills necessary for long-term sustainability and discuss the role of interdisciplinary approaches in promoting individual and collective behavioural changes.

pmc-11682759.title: Hematological and thermographical changes in rat’s model exposed to long-term RF modulated signals
pmc-11682759.creator: Omar B Aghaa, Bashaer K Hameed
pmc-11682759.description: Background:Long-term exposure to LTE signals at different frequencies has become a crucial problem in our daily life.Aim:The aim of the study to figure out the thermal influence of LTE signals (850 MHz, 1800 MHz, and 2600 MHz) on hematological values in rat’s model during different periods.

pmc-12704704.title: Gamified Simulation for Onboarding Health Care Teams in Emergency Care: Development and Preliminary Feasibility Study
pmc-12704704.creator: Stephane Gobron, Antoine Lestrade, Artan Sadiku, Alexandre Bentvelzen, Leila Ait Kaci, Jean-Michel Carrier, Emmanuelle Guyot, Pierre-Nicolas Carron, Javad Sarvestan
pmc-12704704.description: BackgroundHigh staff turnover is a widespread issue across nearly all hospital departments, often exceeding 20% annually. This constant flux disrupts continuity of care and creates a recurring challenge: how to rapidly integrate new employees into complex clinical environments, both physically and functionally. Traditional onboarding methods struggle to meet this demand, particularly in services operating 24/7, such as emergency departments (EDs).

pmc-12732745.title: Who Benefits from Barefooting? The Key Role of Baseline Wellbeing in Psychophysical Restoration
pmc-12732745.creator: Aurelia De Lorenzo, Samuele Berteotti, Fabrizia Giannotta, Emanuela Rabaglietti
pmc-12732745.description: Nature-based activities have been linked to psychophysical restoration, but the role of individual baseline conditions in predicting recovery remains unclear. This study examined whether baseline stress levels and mental wellbeing influence psychophysical recovery after an immersive barefooting experience, and whether sociodemographic factors (sex and education) and access to green spaces moderate these effects.

pmc-12776240.title: Development and validation of a novel prognostic signature for osteosarcoma
pmc-12776240.creator: Xiaowei Wang, Xingyu Zhu, Weiwei Li
pmc-12776240.description: BackgroundOsteosarcoma (OS) is a primary malignant bone tumor known for its aggressive nature and high potential for metastasis, primarily impacting adolescents and young adults. Few studies have focused on discovering gene signatures that effectively guide treatment strategies and predict outcomes in OS. The study aimed to create a prognostic model to predict OS patient survival.

pmc-13230640.title: Controlling the structural, optical, and dielectric properties of PVP/NaAlg-MWCNT flexible nanocomposites for next-generation electronics
pmc-13230640.creator: A. A. Al-Muntaser, Eman Alzahrani, Turki Alkathiri, Sultan Albarakati, Ahmed F. Almutairi, Saleh Aldwais, G. M. Asnag, A. Y. Yassin
pmc-13230640.description: In this study, nanocomposites based on polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and sodium alginate (NaAlg) in a 30/70 wt% ratio were successfully prepared using the solution casting method and reinforced with multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). The effect of MWCNT incorporation on the structural, optical, dielectric, and electrical properties of the pristine PVP/NaAlg blends was comprehensively investigated.

pmc-13540031.title: Targeting Inflammation in Atherosclerosis: Mechanistic Rationale, Clinical Trials, and Regulatory Considerations
pmc-13540031.creator: Lazar Mandinov, Chris A. Learn
pmc-13540031.description: Atherosclerosis remains the leading cause of global mortality, most commonly manifesting as ischemic heart disease, stroke, and peripheral arterial disease. Although age-adjusted cardiovascular mortality has declined in many developed nations, the global burden of atherosclerotic disease continues to rise due to population aging and growth.

pmc-13585425.title: Synergistic inhibition of Notch signaling and forced cell cycle re-entry drive Müller glia reprogramming in uninjured mouse retina
pmc-13585425.creator: Baoshan Liao, Chengshang Lyu, Yuqing Jiang, Shanggong Liu, Waiho Wong, Jiadong Zhang, Hoyin Tsang, Junxi Xie, Lingxi Chen, Qinrong Zhang, Wenjun Xiong, Xiaorong Liu, Baoshan Liao, Chengshang Lyu, Yuqing Jiang, Shanggong Liu, Waiho Wong, Jiadong Zhang, Hoyin Tsang, Junxi Xie, Lingxi Chen, Qinrong Zha
pmc-13585425.description: In regenerative species, such as teleost fish, Müller glia (MG) autonomously re-enter the cell cycle after injury and give rise to functional retinal neurons. In contrast, the loss of retinal neurons in mammals is irreversible due to the limited proliferative and regenerative ability of MG.
